label: GO step (choice phase) detector
explanation: Fires on every GO step (100% of GO steps, all rel positions, both actions) at nearly constant magnitude (mean 7.04, max 7.46; per-cell activations 0.86-1.00 of max). It almost never fires at D1 (0.5%, tiny activations ~0.01 of max) and never at D2. Precision 1.0 and recall 0.995 on dev; the misses are near-zero D1 activations and hold 0.0% of the mass. Rate at GO does not depend on choice, reward history, transition, good state, or stay/switch; it simply marks the go-signal step. In the example windows magnitude is a little lower (~0.86-0.91) during long rewarded streaks and higher (~0.97-1.0) around unrewarded or rare trials and switches, but this is only a small modulation I saw in examples and did not test systematically. Uses only observed inputs (the go signal).

issues: The claims check out. Dev profile: GO is active on 380619 of 380619 steps (rate 1.000) and holds 100% of the activation mass. Firing is uniform across rel -3 to +1 (about 0.20 of the mass each) and is flat across action, state, common, reward, prev_reward and stay (lift 1.0x everywhere).
Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.994, F1 0.997, mass recall 0.99993, correlation 0.9995, and zero false positives.

The missed activations (2411 test steps) are tiny D1 activations of about 0.00 to 0.05 of max and hold 0.0% of the mass. They are slightly more common at the first D1 of an episode (in_rew == -1: 472 of 492 active) and at unrewarded D1s. Because they carry negligible magnitude, this is not a meaningful counterexample class.
Small wording issue: 'never at D2' is really 5 active D2 steps out of 380619 on dev, with negligible activation. That is effectively never.
The magnitude modulation the explanation mentions (lower in long rewarded streaks) was not tested systematically. The explanation hedges it correctly, and it does not affect the binary label.
